terms.meaning: a hosted database service where the app stores its data
a local file of keys and addresses that a program reads when it starts
a named group of rows in the database, similar to a spreadsheet tab

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Loading settings and checking the connection
sections.what: Loads the project's environment settings, then prints whether the database client is configured for this run.
sections.why: Likely reason: the database client needs its address and key loaded before it is used.
sections.watch_out: Imports can run before the settings load in some setups, so if results look wrong, check the configured flag first.

sections.name: tables
sections.title: List of database tables to check
sections.what: Lists the sixteen table names the app stores data in, such as tasks, goals, internships and certifications.
sections.why: Likely reason: one list lets the script check every table in a single run.
sections.watch_out: A table missing from this list is not checked, so update the list when a new table is added.

sections.name: checkTables
sections.title: Counting rows in each table
sections.what: Goes through each table, counts its rows, and prints the count with a couple of sample names. An error for one table is printed and the run continues.
sections.why: Likely reason: a live check that shows which tables exist and which hold data.
sections.watch_out: It reads every row of each table, which can be slow on large tables. It does not change any data.

summary: A manual script that counts the rows in sixteen live database tables and prints any errors it finds.
purpose: Confirm the online database is reachable and see how much data each table holds.
why: Likely reason: a health check after the app's data was moved to Supabase. Reason not stated in the code.
how: 1. Loads the project's environment settings. 2. Prints whether the database client is configured. 3. Goes through the table name list one at a time, reading all rows and counting them. 4. Prints the count and a few sample names for each table, or the error message.
inputs: The environment settings file in the project folder, and the table name list written in the script.
outputs: Console lines for each table showing a count, sample entries, or an error message. Nothing is changed.
risks: Reads every row of every table, so large tables take time. It uses the database credentials in the settings file, so run it only against the project you intend to check.
debug: If every table shows an error, check that the settings file has the database address and key. If the configured flag prints false, check that the settings load before the database client is used. If one table fails, check its name against the database.
